issues.problem: Mapping cone written with differential (c,x) -> (-dc, phi(c)+dx), while the block cites Weibel and Boe, who both use (-db, dc - f(b)) (Weibel Def. 1.5.1, Boe Def. 6.2.2). The page's later connecting-map claims follow Weibel's sign.
issues.fix: Switched to Weibel's sign, wrote out the d^2 = 0 check, added a conventions row on shifts and cones, and updated the cone check to the new sign.

issues.problem: Connecting map of 0->D->cone->C[-1]->0 given as H_n(phi) 'possibly up to sign'. That is the wrong index: H_n(C[-1]) = H_{n-1}(C).
issues.fix: Now states H_{n-1}(phi), exactly (Weibel Lemma 1.5.3).

issues.problem: Claimed Holanda-Miranda-Neto's Burch rings are 'defined by conditions on minimal resolutions' and that their Ext/Tor vanishing theorems 'are statements that certain Betti numbers vanish'. Neither claim is in the paper (its §1 cites [20] for Burch rings and does not define them this way), and the second is false in general.
issues.fix: Removed both claims; the block now only says their freeness criteria deduce freeness from Ext/Tor vanishing.

issues.problem: The argument that Z/2 is not a summand of (Z/4)^n did not work as written: an element of order 2 in the summand is twice an element of the free module, not of the summand.
issues.fix: Rewrote it with the projection onto the summand: e = 2y gives e = pi(e) = 2 pi(y) = 0. Added a brute-force check.

issues.problem: The lead-in said the sequence 'is named in opposite ways', but every row said 'quotient first'. The Quick row also misreported the source: Quick 19 calls 0->A->B->M->0 an extension of M by A, then states the splitting criterion with Ext(A,M), which slips the variance.
issues.fix: Rewrote the lead-in. Added an nLab row and a Wikipedia group-extension row (new source w-ge, which notes that the reversed phrasing is also used). The Quick row now describes the slip accurately.

issues.problem: The informal exact-structure definition omitted closure under isomorphism and the identities axiom, and said 'short exact sequences' for an additive category. It said 'pullback, pushout' without saying which class is stable under which operation. The subgroup claim was the writer's own argument.
issues.fix: Restated it following BBH Definition 3.2 (equivalent to Quillen): admissible monos stable under pushout, admissible epis under pullback, kernel-cokernel pairs in the additive case. Cited BBH Remark 3.6 (closed subbifunctor of Ext^1) for the subgroup claim, and described BBH's actual use (relative Betti numbers, rank invariant).

issues.problem: 'Free abelian groups do not (the cokernel of 2 is not free)': inside free groups that map does have a categorical cokernel (0). The real failure is that coimage differs from image.
issues.fix: Rephrased with both points.

issues.problem: Said the cochain complex Hom(P,B) 'is a simplicial abelian group' whose homotopy groups are the Ext groups. Dold-Kan needs a non-negatively graded chain complex.
issues.fix: Now shifts by n and truncates, giving pi_i = Ext^{n-i} and pi_0 = Ext^n, which matches nLab and the r/math answer.

issues.problem: For the self-intersection of x = 0 the Tor groups have infinite length, so Serre's formula does not apply; the text implied that the higher Tor groups 'record the excess'. The vanishing condition was also stated in a form not in the cited source.
issues.fix: Added the infinite-length remark. The vanishing condition now follows Wikipedia: locally cut out by regular sequences and meeting properly.

issues.problem: The cosyzygy C^{n-1} was not defined, and the indexing was ambiguous.
issues.fix: Defined C^{n-1} as the image of I^{n-1} -> I^n (C^{-1} = N), wrote out the length-n resolution, and cited Weibel 4.1.11.

issues.fix: Cited stacks-hom (Lemma 12.5.17 has a proof; 12.5.20 follows from 12.5.19) and Weibel Ch.1 (1.3.2, Ex. 1.3.3). Lemma numbers added to the theorem blocks.

issues.problem: Arapura (Example 5.12) only says that f.g. abelian groups lack enough injectives; the page attributed 'no non-zero injectives at all' to him. Bannister was said to use the adjoint principle 'repeatedly'; it is his Lemma 3.22.
issues.fix: The attribution now matches Arapura, and the stronger claim is proved on the page. Cited Weibel Prop. 2.3.10 and Cor. 2.3.11 and Crawley-Boevey §2.4.

issues.problem: 'Weibel Corollary 3.2.10' was given as the localisation statement. It is flat base change for a flat algebra T.
issues.fix: Now cites it with T = S^{-1}R.

issues.problem: Said Stacks Lemma 10.109.7 'records' that f.g. projectives over local rings are free. 10.109.7 is about resolutions by finite free modules and uses Lemma 10.78.2. The Betti and pd facts had no source.
issues.fix: Cited Weibel Prop. 4.3.11 and 4.4.11 (new source weibel4) and corrected the Stacks description.

issues.problem: Said BBH 'compare the global dimension of incidence algebras with their representation dimension'. BBH need finite global dimension of an exact structure and relate a relative (add X) global dimension of grid incidence algebras to representation dimension.
issues.fix: Rephrased to match BBH.

issues.problem: Parts 2-3 (injective dimension via R/J; global dimension as sup of id) were cited only to Stacks §10.109, which has no injective dimension.
issues.fix: Added Weibel Lemmas 4.1.6 and 4.1.11 and Theorem 4.1.2, and Wikipedia Global dimension.

issues.problem: Bannister's Lemma 3.27 was described as identifying two definitions of derived limits; it compares lim^s of a sum with the sum of lim^s via the universal property (Fact 3.26 is the uniqueness statement).
issues.fix: Rewrote the sentence and added Weibel 2.1.4/2.4.7 for universality.

issues.problem: 'Over a local ring or a PID f.g. projectives are free' was cited to cb and boe, neither of which says it.

issues.problem: Cited Arapura Lemma 5.29 for both invariants and coinvariants. It covers only coinvariants.
